% A guard: it checks a case that the fix of the files read with the
% primitive \input must not break.
% A shortened copy of LaTeX's dvipsnam.def in a subfolder, read with the
% primitive \input after xcolor. The copy names itself
% \ProvidesFile{dvipsnam.def}, so tex4ht reads dvipsnam.4ht, as for the
% tree's file. As in the PDF, a named color keeps its value.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{xcolor}
\makeatletter
\input test-priminput/vendor/dvipsnam.def
\makeatother
\begin{document}
\textcolor[named]{BrickRed}{Brick red text.}
\end{document}
